data.title: Mobile layout, README and deployment to GitHub Pages

events.line: Accepted, I will study the code and write the statement of task 4
events.text:
Write the statement of task 4, the last in the series, for the split-bill project. Tasks 1–3 are done and committed, read the code yourself, especially the styles, the page markup, the interface files, the package description and the ignore lists.

Task: a mobile layout from 360 px and wider and a README with a description, a screenshot or GIF and run instructions; a GitHub Actions workflow for deployment to GitHub Pages. Turning Pages on in the repository settings will be done by the human, so write in the README and in the report what to click.

The human's decisions are made in advance: the statement is approved, resolve the forks yourself and put them into the section "Accepted decisions". No new runtime dependencies and no CSS frameworks. The layout: at 360 px width there is no horizontal scroll, the fields and buttons are comfortable for a finger (a touch target of about 44 px), long names and amounts wrap, on a wide screen a neat column of limited width. Verifiability: an automatic check in the browser at 360, 768 and 1280 px that the document width does not exceed the window width with a filled bill with long names; Chromium and Playwright are in the environment, but do not add Playwright to the project and make check must not depend on it, the check script is run from a temporary directory.

Screenshot: a PNG taken by Playwright at a mobile width with a filled example bill without personal data lies in the repository, the README links to it by a relative path. The base path: the site will live in a subdirectory, do not hardcode the owner's name anywhere; decide how to set up the Vite base path, and check that development, preview, build and tests do not break.

The workflow: run on push to main and manually; Node 22 with the npm cache; install dependencies, then make check, then the dist artifact and deployment with the official GitHub Pages actions with minimal permissions (read content, write to Pages and the id token) and a limit of concurrent runs for Pages. The action versions are the current major tags that exist on GitHub.

The README in Russian: what it is and who it is for, a screenshot, features (participants, expenses, the minimal number of transfers with an explanation, the "Share" link without a server), how to run locally, how the project is organized, deployment to Pages and what the human should click, where the address will appear. No server addresses, keys or personal data, the site address as a template. Briefly mention the limitations: a very large bill may not fit into a link, and the exact minimum of transfers is guaranteed up to 16 participants with a non-zero balance.

Follow the project rules; in the styles introduce custom properties for repeated values. Name what does not belong to the task in the section "Out of scope". Known and out of scope: the aria-live area on the whole summary section.

events.line: Here is the statement: fluid layout, workflow, README
events.text:
The statement is ready. Goal: the app is comfortable to open from a phone from 360 px and from a computer, it deploys itself to GitHub Pages from main, and the README explains what it is, how to run it and how to turn Pages on.

What I checked on a copy of the project, I did not change the project itself. Now at 360 px with long names the page scrolls sideways: the document width is 495 at a window width of 360. Long names without spaces stick out in the list rows, the checkbox labels and the field group, whose minimum width by default equals the content width. Buttons and fields are 37 px high, checkboxes 13 by 13 px. The proposed set of rules removes the scroll at 360, 768 and 1280 px and makes fields and buttons 44 px high; without a ban on shrinking the "Remove" button in the lists shrinks and wraps. With the Vite config and a relative base path make check is green, the paths in the built page are relative, the build works from a subdirectory. The current major tags of the actions are found through the list of tags of the repositories.

Plan. First, the styles: at the beginning of the file introduce custom properties for colors, radii, the gap between sections, the column width and the touch target of 44 px and move all rules to them; enable box-sizing border-box for all, wrapping of long words on the whole page body, zero minimum width for the field group, full width for text fields and select lists, a minimum height of 44 px for fields and buttons; make checkboxes flex containers, so that the whole label becomes the touch zone; in the lists align the rows to the center and forbid shrinking of the buttons. The layout is fluid, media queries only when needed, do not touch the markup and the page. Second, the Vite config with a relative base path and a Russian comment on "why": the app opens from any subdirectory without the owner's name in the code, the state lies in the address fragment. The file is exactly js, because ts outside tsconfig breaks the linter. Third, the deployment workflow: run on push to main and manually, permissions exactly for reading content, writing to Pages and the id token, a limit of concurrent runs, a build job (checkout, Node 22 with the npm cache, install dependencies, make check, which already builds dist, configure Pages, upload the artifact) and a deployment job with the environment github-pages. Fourth, the screenshot and the README: a script from a temporary directory shoots the built app at a width of 390 px with a double pixel density, the example is Ann, Ben, Clara, Dan and three expenses, the size up to about 600 KB; the README with sections about the purpose, the screenshot, features, local run, the project structure, deployment to Pages and limitations.

The layout check script lies outside the project. It builds the app, puts it into a subdirectory, starts a static server and in Chromium fills the bill with long names and a huge amount at the widths 360, 768 and 1280. It checks that there is no horizontal scroll, no element goes beyond the right edge, fields, buttons and checkboxes are not lower than 44 px, the button text is not cut and does not wrap. At 360 px it additionally checks the states after "Share" and after opening a garbage fragment, at 1280 — that the column is not wider than 640 px and stands in the center. There must be no page errors or failed requests.

Accepted decisions: a relative base path in the Vite config, not a flag and not a hardcoded subdirectory; there is no separate build step in the workflow, because make check already builds dist, and the checks are not bypassed; permissions at the level of the whole workflow, as in the official template; a fluid layout without media queries and without new dependencies; wrapping of long words by one rule on the page body; the check and screenshot scripts lie outside the repository, only the PNG goes into it; three commits — styles, config with the deployment workflow, README with the screenshot.

Done criteria: the check script passes at three widths, including "Share" and a broken link at 360; make check is green, formatting changes nothing; the paths in the built page are relative, the app works from a subdirectory; the development mode opens the app; the deployment workflow matches the listed, the action tags exist, the YAML parses; the screenshot is 390 or 780 px wide and up to about 600 KB, the README links to it by a relative path; the README has all the sections, the owner's name is hardcoded nowhere, there are no keys or personal data; the existing tests were not changed and pass, the interface files and the page were not changed. There are no new tests: there is no new logic in the task.

Out of scope: the aria-live area on the summary section; the same caption on all expense delete buttons; no favicon; no formatting check in make check and CI; CI does not run on pull requests; the Vite config is not checked by tsc. What the human should click: in the repository settings open Pages, in the build section choose the source "GitHub Actions", then push to main or run the workflow manually on the main branch; the address will appear in the Pages settings and in the run summary of the "Deploy" job.

events.line: Accepted. I make the layout, the workflow, the README and the screenshot
events.text:
Do task 4 of the split-bill project by the approved statement. Tasks 1–3 are committed. Do not commit — the lead will do it, he will split the work into three commits: styles; the Vite config with the deployment workflow; the README with the screenshot. Read the project rules.

Put the layout check and screenshot scripts into a temporary directory, not into the repository. The analyst left trial scripts and a copy of the project there, they can be taken as a base. Playwright is taken from the tools installed in the environment, the browsers are preinstalled; do not add Playwright to the project.

The content of the statement. Styles: custom properties for colors, radii, gaps, the column width and the touch target of 44 px; box-sizing border-box, wrapping of long words on the whole body, zero minimum width for the field group, full width for text fields and select lists, a minimum height of 44 px for fields and buttons, checkboxes as flex containers, alignment of list rows and a ban on shrinking buttons; delete the duplicate of the rule for read-only fields; do not touch the markup and the page. The Vite config: a relative base path with a Russian comment on "why". The deployment workflow: push to main and a manual run, Node 22 with the npm cache, install, make check, configure Pages, upload the dist artifact, a deployment job; permissions exactly for reading content, writing to Pages and the id token; a limit of concurrent runs; the current major tags of the actions, which must be rechecked before finishing. The screenshot: the built app at a width of 390 px with a double density, the example Ann, Ben, Clara, Dan and three expenses, the summary and the block "How it is calculated" are visible, up to about 600 KB. The README in Russian of seven sections: purpose, screenshot, features, local run, the project structure, deployment to Pages with what to click, and limitations. The site address in the README is a template, without keys and personal data; after the edits run the formatting.

The layout check script must reproducibly build the app, put it into a subdirectory, start a static server and in Chromium at the widths 360, 768 and 1280 fill the bill with long names and a huge amount. It checks the absence of horizontal scroll, elements going beyond the right edge, the height of fields, buttons and checkboxes not lower than 44 px, unwrappable button text. At 360 px the states after "Share" and after a garbage fragment are additionally checked, at 1280 — the column is not wider than 640 px and in the center. There must be no page errors or failed requests, a 404 on the favicon is acceptable explicitly, with a comment. The script prints the result per width and returns a non-zero code on failure.

Done criteria: the script passes at three widths; make check is green, formatting changes nothing; the paths in the built page are relative, the app works from a subdirectory; the development mode opens; the deployment workflow matches the listed, the YAML parses; the screenshot is 390 or 780 px wide; the README has all the sections, the owner's name is not in it and not in the workflow; the existing tests and interface files were not changed. Out of scope: the aria-live area on the summary, the same caption of the expense delete buttons, no favicon, no formatting check in make check and CI, CI does not run on pull requests.

In the answer write what was done by the points, deviations with the reason, the result of make check and of the check script per width, the size and width of the screenshot and the commands to run the check script.

events.line: Here you are. Task 4 is ready, the layout script passes at three widths
events.text:
Task 4 is done by the statement, no deviations. make check is green: 270 tests in ten files and the build. The layout check script passes at 360, 768 and 1280 px. Nothing is committed.

Done by files. The styles file is rewritten by the plan: at the beginning custom properties for colors (including the warning), radii, the gap between sections, the column width, the touch target of 44 px and the checkbox size, all rules are moved to them; added are box-sizing, wrapping of long words on the body, zero minimum width for the field group, full width for text fields and select lists, a minimum height of fields and buttons, checkboxes as flex containers with a touch zone of 44 px, alignment of the lists, a ban on shrinking buttons; the duplicate of the rule is removed, there are no media queries, I did not touch the markup and the tests. The Vite config is new, with a relative base path and a Russian comment. The deployment workflow is made exactly by the plan; the action tags are checked, checkout and setup-node have v7, configure-pages v6, upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages v5; the YAML parses, the triggers are push to main and a manual run. The README has all seven sections, a search for github.io finds only the owner template in the README and in the config comments. The screenshot is a PNG of 780 by 4790 (width 390 at a double density), 328 KB; on it the example Ann, Ben, Clara, Dan, three expenses, three transfers and "How it is calculated", without an address bar.

Checks. Formatting repeated changes nothing. The build gives relative paths. The development mode answers 200. The check script: at 360 px everything is fine (an empty page, a filled bill, after "Share", a field with a long link, a message about a broken link, page and request errors), at 768 and 1280 px too, at 1280 the column is not wider than 640 px and in the center. On the old CSS the script fails: at 360 px the document width is 594, a button goes beyond the edge, fields and buttons are 36.8 px, so it really catches the problem.

How to run (the scripts lie outside the repository). The check script builds the app itself, copies dist into a subdirectory, starts a static server and returns a non-zero code on any failure. The screenshot script rebuilds the app and overwrites the shot, by default with a double density.

Nuances. For "Share" the script checks two cases: the usual one and one with the clipboard substituted by a refusal, so that the field with a long link appears. A 404 on the favicon is explicitly allowed, with a comment, there was none in the run. Out of scope remain the aria-live area on the summary, the same caption of the expense delete buttons, the absence of a favicon, the absence of a formatting check in make check and CI and the absence of CI on pull requests.

events.line: Accepted. I will check the layout, the workflow and the README against the criteria
events.text:
Review the uncommitted changes for task 4: the new Vite config, the deployment workflow, the README and the screenshot (look at the picture). Tasks 1–3 were committed earlier, review only task 4. Do experiments only in a copy in a temporary directory, do not change files.

Task: a mobile layout from 360 px and a README with a description, a screenshot and a run; a GitHub Actions workflow for deployment to GitHub Pages. Turning Pages on will be done by the human, the README says what to click.

The key decisions of the statement: a fluid layout without media queries and CSS frameworks, custom properties, box-sizing border-box, wrapping of long words on the body, touch targets of 44 px, checkboxes with a label as the touch zone, do not touch the markup; the Vite config with a relative base path without the owner's name; the deployment workflow on push to main and manually, Node 22 with a cache, install, make check, configure Pages, upload the artifact, deployment, minimal permissions and a limit of concurrent runs; a screenshot of 390 px with a double density with the example Ann, Ben, Clara, Dan; the README in Russian. The layout check script lies outside the repository, it can be run: it builds the app itself, puts it into a subdirectory, starts a server and checks the widths 360, 768 and 1280.

Done criteria: the script passes at three widths with all measurements, including "Share" and a broken link at 360 and a column no wider than 640 px at 1280; make check is green, formatting changes nothing; the paths in the built page are relative, the app works from a subdirectory; the development mode opens the app; the deployment workflow matches the listed, the action tags exist, the YAML is correct; the screenshot is 390 or 780 px wide and up to about 600 KB without personal data; the README has all the sections, the owner's name is hardcoded nowhere, the facts in it match the code — the commands from the package description and the Makefile, the directories, the limit of 16 participants, the code length limit; the existing tests, the interface files and the page were not changed.

Check the styles especially: whether there are regressions in the error and success messages, the plate, the hiding of elements and the link field, whether it became worse on a wide screen. Check the deployment workflow: whether it will work on GitHub, whether make exists on ubuntu-latest, whether a lock file is needed for the npm cache, the github-pages environment. Check the README: whether it is clear to a person who sees the project for the first time. The project rules — as usual.

events.line: Looking at the CSS and the screenshot
events.text: Next I look at the whole CSS and the screenshot.

events.line: Accepted: nothing serious, three small things can be left unfixed
events.text:
ACCEPTED. I checked only task 4. There are no serious remarks, below is what was checked and three small things that may be left unfixed.

Done criteria. The layout check script passes at 360, 768 and 1280 px; at 360 "Share", the field with a long link and a broken link pass, at 1280 the column passes the check. make check is green: 270 tests and a build without errors; the formatting check says all files are formatted, including YAML and README. The resources in the built page are linked by relative paths, the app opens from a subdirectory. The dev server starts on the standard port and serves the page. The deployment workflow triggers on push to main and manually, uses Node 22 with the npm cache, the steps go in the needed order, there are exactly three permissions, the limit of runs by the pages group without cancelling the running one, the deployment job has the github-pages environment and the address from the deployment step. The action tags are checked against the list of repository tags and exist, make exists on ubuntu-latest, the workflow should work on GitHub. The screenshot is a PNG of 780 by 4790 (390 px at a double density), 335 KB, without text metadata, it shows Ann, Ben, Clara, Dan; the README links to it by a relative path. The README has all the sections, the github.io domain appears only as a template, there are no keys, server addresses or personal data; the commands match the package description and the Makefile, the directories match the tree and the linter rule, the limit of 16 participants matches the constant, and the message about an approximate calculation is output in the explanation text. In the working copy only the styles file is changed, the tests, the interface files and the page are not touched.

Style regressions. The hiding rule is still the last one and by specificity overrides the others. The rules of the error and success messages did not change, only the colors are moved into variables. The plate button does not shrink. Removing the separate rule for the read-only field is justified: the width and box-sizing are now set by the shared rules. On a wide screen it did not get worse.

Small remarks, optional. First: in the README the phrase that the app "will open" at the local address is inaccurate — the dev server does not open the browser itself, it is better to write "open the address in a browser". Second: the comment in the styles about a name without spaces reads with a hitch, better "Without this, a long name without spaces will stretch the page wider than the phone screen". Third: the screenshot on the GitHub page will take about 2400 px in height; if a compact README is needed, one can shoot only the top part or the summary.

By the way, not on task 4: the bill encoding does not check the code length limit, so for a too large bill "Share" will silently give a link that then opens as corrupted. This is the behavior of task 3, and the README describes it honestly.

events.line: Accepted. I will fix two comments, then make check
events.text:
Make two small text fixes in the uncommitted task 4 of the split-bill project. The review accepted the task. Do not commit and change nothing else.

First: in the README the comment that the app "will open" at the local address is inaccurate — the dev server does not open the browser itself. Rewrite it more precisely, for example: "the dev server at the local address — open the address in a browser".

Second: in the styles file the comment "A name without spaces otherwise will stretch the page…" reads with a hitch. Rewrite it correctly: "Without this, a long name without spaces will stretch the page wider than the phone screen" or close in meaning.

Then run the formatting and make check, it must be green. The answer is one or two lines.

events.line: Done. Both comments are fixed, make check is green
events.text: Both fixes are made. In the README the comment now says that the dev server runs at the local address and the address must be opened in a browser. In the styles file the comment is now: "Without this, a long name without spaces will stretch the page wider than the phone screen." Formatting and make check passed, make check finished with exit code 0. Nothing is committed and nothing else was changed.

events.line: Checks passed, only the dev server was not started
events.text:
CHECKS PASSED. I did not change or add tests, I did not touch files in the repository.

I read the layout check script entirely, everything from the first criterion is checked in it. A bill of five participants is filled in, including a name of 40 letters without spaces and "Konstantin Konstantinopolsky-Vanya", amounts 1500, 349.90 and 99999999999.99 with long payers; the summary with transfers and "How it is calculated" fall into this filling. The script checks the absence of horizontal scroll, the right edge of every visible element, a height of at least 44 px for buttons, text fields, select lists and checkboxes, that the button text is not cut and does not wrap; at 360 px the same after "Share" with the link field on a clipboard refusal and with a garbage fragment with the message plate; at 1280 a column no wider than 640 px in the center; page errors and failed requests, a 404 on the favicon is ignored on purpose.

By the criteria. First: the script returned 0, at three widths all measurements are fine. Second: make check returned 0, formatting changed nothing. Third: the resources in the built page are relative, the script serves the build from a subdirectory without errors. Fourth: I did not start the dev server on the standard port, this remained unchecked; the Vite config contains only a relative base path, the port was not changed. Fifth: the deployment workflow satisfies the criterion point by point — triggers, Node 22 with the npm cache, the order of steps, exactly three permissions, the limit of runs by the pages group, the action tags exist, the YAML parses, two jobs — build and deployment; there is no actionlint in the environment, I could not run it. Sixth: the screenshot is a PNG of 780 by 4790, 336 KB, it shows a filled example with Ann, Ben, Clara and Dan, three expenses, the summary and "How it is calculated", without an address bar and personal data; the README links to it by a relative path. Seventh: the README sections are in place, the github.io domain appears only as a template, there are no keys or personal data; the commands from the README exist in the package description and the Makefile, all paths from the section about the project structure exist. Eighth: only the styles file is changed, added are the Vite config, the deployment workflow, the README and the screenshot, the interface files and the page are not touched, the existing tests pass.

Additionally I ran a copy of the script at a width of 320 px with the same measurements, including "Share", the link field and a garbage fragment: there is no overflow. A long amount in the summary and in the breakdown "How it is calculated" is part of the filled bill, the measurements at 360, 768, 1280 and 320 px are clean.
